name: Singaporean Mahjong
description: Singaporean Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with animal bonus tile rules and local scoring conventions. It uses an expanded 148-tile composition and keeps the standard draw-discard claim rhythm.

overview.description: Singaporean Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with animal bonus tile rules and local scoring conventions. It uses an expanded 148-tile composition and keeps the standard draw-discard claim rhythm.

history.origins: Singaporean Mahjong developed as a regional profile with animal bonus interactions and local scoring styles.
timeline: Modern era: published rulesets standardize bonus and scoring treatment.
history.cultural: It is widely played socially in Singapore and diaspora communities.
history.evolution: Animal bonus rules and local scoring distinguish this profile from many Chinese regional variants.

setup.deck: 148-tile Mahjong set with suited tiles, honors, flowers/seasons, and animal bonus tiles.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 tiles; dealer receives 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand and satisfy active Singaporean scoring and bonus rules.
rules.gameplay: Players draw and discard in turn while claiming legal sets by priority rules. Bonus/animal tiles are resolved by profile conventions and can affect scoring outcomes.
keyRules: Draw then discard is the core loop.
Claim legality and priority determine interruptions.
Bonus and animal resolution follows profile scoring conventions.

strategy.basic: Build efficient waits while respecting defensive discard timing.
strategy.intermediate: Track visible bonuses and opponent tempo to avoid feeding high-value lines.
strategy.advanced: Balance completion speed, bonus value, and defense based on visible threat signals.
tips: Do not chase bonus value at the cost of hand efficiency.
Switch to safer discards when opponents reveal coherent routes.

synthesis.shortDescription: Singaporean Mahjong uses a 148-tile set with animal-bonus scoring mechanics.
